main_body: Open wooden gong frame: a top crossbeam, two vertical posts, two base blocks, and a hanging round gold gong disc between the posts
top_band: Crossbeam: light pinkish-brown top band at rows ~2-5, then a step to a darker brown front face at rows ~6-8. Each base block has a lighter top at rows ~26-28 and a dark front at rows ~29-31.
evidence: In a column through the crossbeam I meet a light top band (~rows 3-5), a lighter front-edge step, then a dark front face with a shadow under the overhang (rows 6-8). The base blocks repeat this: a lighter top (rows 26-28), then a dark front (rows 29-31). So the beam and base show horizontal top faces, as the frame kind requires. The posts are plain vertical members and the gong is a vertical disc. The tops are foreshortened and modest at about 3 rows each, but both are clearly more than a rim line.

style.evidence: The gong has about 5 yellow steps with a highlight sweep and dithered shading. The wood has a light top, a mid tone and a dark underside, with outlines in dark brown rather than black. The posts are narrow, fairly plain two-tone strips and the base blocks have little grain, so it is slightly thinner than the roofed well and the stall. It is still acceptable next to the references, with no sticker look and no large flat areas.
